pool.drawSite: npcStructure.js:424 T[cat__cond__rank] (registry; ids are `<category>__<condition>__<rank>.<field>`; condition keys: governance_fractured, corruption, food_crisis, economic_stress, contested, stable — see getPrimaryCondition; keyDeclares should record what each condition key guarantees, e.g. food_crisis → hunger family; corruption → crime)
pool.note: Condition is getPrimaryCondition's first hit: governance_fractured = publicLegitimacy.governanceFractured (legitimacy score < 30, NOT the politically_fractured stress kind; no atom); corruption = criminalCaptureState corrupted|capture (→ crime, no factsOf home); food_crisis = foodSecurity label famine|deficit (→ hunger per brief, BUT crisisKind.js counts a deficit toward hunger only while some crisis is active, so a deficit with no stress kind is not hunger to the reader); economic_stress = prosperity struggling|poor|subsist (no atom); contested = publicLegitimacy.isContested (no atom); stable = the residual — it does NOT exclude active crisis kinds (a siege with legitimacy and food intact lands here), so the stable lines that assert a stable/well-ordered/low-risk settlement are declared crisis "calm". The category key guarantees the NPC (criminal → crime; magic → magic, via worldLaw.allowsRole's magic gate). crafts__* lines are verbatim copies of economy__*. WRONG TODAY: other__{corruption,food_crisis,economic_stress,contested}__* are the other__stable__* text copied by the fill loop at npcStructure.js:387-391, so under a corruption/food/economic/contested condition they print "in a stable settlement" / "in stable conditions" — the calm declarations on 264-287 record that contradiction against their own key. Also: the subordinate texts never use reg()'s replace() fallback (every reg passes an explicit sub).

rows.text: Holds the seat in name, but fewer people come when called, and some orders go unanswered.
Get the seat obeyed again before the week is out, or find a quiet way out of it.
Cannot mend what is broken without bringing to light the quiet deals that keep the place running now.
Holds an office under a seat that fewer people now obey; the office is only as strong as the seat.
Keep their office through the collapse without being seen with the failing seat or its rivals.
Moving to protect the office looks like a grab; standing still means falling with the seat.
Holds the seat while criminals pay for favours close to it; some orders that matter are settled elsewhere.
Keep the seat running without crossing the people whose payments keep it running.
Cannot move against the criminals without cutting off the payments the seat now runs on.
Holds an office among officials who take bribes; not one of the takers, but working beside them.
Show their own books are clean while the people above them take payments.
Any honest inquiry needs the help of officials who are themselves on the take.
Holds the seat while the food runs short; how the hunger ends will decide whether the seat is kept.
Get food to every door before a rival for the seat does it first.
Cannot hand out food that is not there, and cannot say how short it is without frightening people further.
Holds an office that is blamed for the shortage but has little say over the food.
Be seen handing out what little there is, and let the blame for the rest go upward.
Being seen to work hard while the food stays short only spreads the blame.
Holds the seat while money is short, and people judge the seat by what it can no longer pay for.
Win the people back with things that cost nothing: fair hearings and quick answers.
Cannot pay for the repairs and relief people want without coin the place does not have.
Holds an office whose purse shrinks with everyone else's.
Become the one person who signs off on every coin the seat still spends.
Every office is after the same few coins; making this one needed means taking from the others.
Holds the seat, but a rival claims it, and the matter is not settled.
Win the doubters back before the challenger to the seat wins them first.
Every hard move wins the rival new supporters; every delay gives the rival time.
Holds an office that hangs on a seat someone else is trying to take.
Stay off both sides of the fight for the seat until it is plain who wins.
Waiting to see who wins keeps the office safe today and earns no thanks from the winner.
Holds the seat, and people accept it; there is room to act, not just to hold on.
Find and mend the seat's weak spot before a rival finds it first.
With nothing pressing, it is hard to win support for mending the weak spots before they break.
Holds an office that runs from day to day, with no crisis to answer.
Do every task the seat hands them so well that the seat cannot do without them.
Good work is expected and goes unnoticed; a mistake is remembered.
Commands those under arms while the seat loses its hold; whoever gives the orders next will want them.
Keep the people under their command together, whoever ends up giving the orders.
Cannot step in to keep order without taking a side in the fight over the seat.
Leads a squad that now takes orders from more than one master.
Stop any faction buying their squad away from them while the seat is broken.
Keeping the squad in hand takes quiet favours that no one can be told about.
Commands those under arms while criminals pay some of the people in their ranks.
Find out which of their own officers are on the take, before the payers notice.
Anyone sent to look into the payments is offered the same coin.
Leads a squad in a force where some officers are known to take bribes.
Keep their own hands clean without catching the eye of the bribers or the inquiry.
Going along too easily or pushing back too hard both draw notice the squad cannot afford.
Keeps order while the food runs short, when hungry crowds are quickest to riot.
Keep the hungry from rioting without striking anyone the crowd will remember.
Enough force to stop a riot can be enough to start the next, and nobody knows beforehand how much is too much.
Leads a squad that keeps order among people who are going hungry.
Hold their patch quiet with too few hands, and start no fight they cannot finish.
Has too few hands for the work, and is judged as though it had enough.
Keeps order while money is short, when trouble grows and the pay for stopping it shrinks.
Be seen enough to stop trouble, and not so much that people start to hate them.
The same lack of coin that stirs the trouble cuts the pay of those sent to stop it.
Leads a squad that is short of pay, gear and hands.
Hide how short of pay and gear their squad has become before someone tests it.
If anyone sees how thin the squad has worn, they will test it.
Commands those under arms while rivals fight over the seat, and each side wants them.
Keep everyone under their command out of the fight for the seat until it is settled.
Keeping those under arms out of the fight takes quiet work that cannot be owned in public.
Leads a squad whose members are being pulled toward one side or the other in the fight for the seat.
Stop their squad splitting into two camps before the fight for the seat is over.
Some of the squad have loyalties of their own, and they do not all point the same way.
Commands those under arms in quiet times; the work is keeping trouble from starting.
Keep the drills, the patrols and the pay going, and the old hands in charge of them.
With nothing threatening, it is hard to win the coin and the say that would be needed if trouble came.
Leads a squad in quiet times, where the work is routine and the risks are low.
Get their squad noticed for doing the dull work well, and earn a patron by it.
Steady work earns no notice; getting ahead takes a crisis or a patron.
Heads the leading house in the trade while the seat fails; deals still get done where orders do not.
Get their trade's new freedoms written down before whoever takes the seat next takes them back.
Taking new freedoms too openly makes whoever next holds the seat see the house as a threat.
Runs a smaller house behind the leading one in the trade while the seat fails.
Take customers from the biggest house in the trade while the seat is too weak to care.
The disorder that lets the house get ahead can just as quickly knock it back.
Heads the leading house in the trade where criminals have deals with those who keep order; honest and protected business are hard to tell apart.
Keep trading without paying the gangs, and without needing their protection either.
Some of the trade's own dealings lean on the same bought officials it must keep clear of.
Runs a smaller house in a trade where many pay the criminals to be left alone.
Be known as the honest dealer without the crooks deciding to make an example of them.
Standing apart from the crooked dealing draws the crooks' eye; going along makes it everyone's habit.
Heads the leading house in the trade while food is short; what it sells, and to whom, is now watched.
Sell what food they hold at a price nobody will hold against them after the shortage.
Every price it sets during the shortage is taken as a side chosen, whatever was meant.
Runs a smaller house in the trade while food is short, with no hand in who gets the food.
Find something else to sell while the food runs short and the big dealers hold it.
What can be sold now depends on what the shortage has pushed aside, and that can change overnight.
Heads the leading house in the trade while money is short; it holds on, but does not grow.
Work out which buyers will still pay next year, and drop the rest before they drag them down.
Keeping the best buyers means dropping others in plain view, and rivals notice the gaps.
Runs a smaller house while money is short and the bigger houses take more of the trade.
Find the small trade the big houses will not bother to fight them for.
The work the big houses leave alone is the work that pays least.
Heads the leading house in the trade while rivals fight over the seat; whoever wins can make or break it.
Lend to both sides of the fight for the seat, so whoever wins owes them.
Keeping friends on both sides means neither side fully trusts the house.
Runs a smaller house that sells to both sides in the fight for the seat.
Keep selling to every faction without any of them treating their goods as its own.
To both sides, staying out of it looks like fear or scheming.
Heads the leading house in the trade in quiet times; its hold is secure and its say is real.
Turn their hold on the trade into a charter, a seat at the table, or a monopoly.
Every new privilege it gathers in plain sight draws the eye of the seat and of its rivals.
Runs a smaller house behind the leading one in quiet times.
Win more custom without treading on the biggest house in the trade.
Growing into the leading house's trade invites a reply; staying out of it means staying small.

Leads the faith while the seat fails, and people bring it the quarrels the seat no longer settles.
Settle the disputes the seat has stopped settling, in the faith's name, and keep doing it afterwards.
Whatever the faith takes on now, whoever next holds the seat firmly may resent and take back.
Serves the faith under its leaders while the seat fails around them.
Keep marrying, burying and comforting their flock while the seat fails around them.
The flock's trust is easy to earn now, but it buys no say once someone holds the seat firmly again.
Leads the faith among officials who take bribes; its good name rests on keeping clear of them.
Keep the faith's name clean while every other office in the place takes payments.
The faith still needs those same officials for its lands and its rights, so it cannot cut them off.
Serves the faith among people who know their officials take bribes.
Earn their flock's trust face to face, so it outlasts their trust in the crooked seat.
Trust won by standing against the crooked officials can fade once honest ones return.
Leads the faith while the food runs short, and its alms are among the few things holding people together.
Feed the hungry from the faith's stores, and make sure everyone knows who fed them.
The faith's stores will run out; feeding its own first, or for show, would be a scandal remembered long after the hunger.
Serves the faith with little of its own to give while the food runs short.
Get their own flock a share of whatever relief there is, and be thanked for it.
Its standing rests on the relief it passes on; if the relief fails, the blame falls on it too.
Leads the faith while money is short; its lands and alms are both a help and a target.
Keep the faith's lands and coin intact without looking rich while the people go short.
Anything it does to guard its own wealth while people go short is seen by all.
Serves the faith on shrinking alms while money is short.
Keep their small charge going on half the alms and none of the help.
With less to give, there is less reason for the post to exist.
Leads the faith while rivals fight over the seat, and both sides want its blessing.
Give no blessing to either claimant until it is plain which one will hold the seat.
The longer it waits to bless one side, the less the blessing will be worth.
Serves the faith under its leaders while rivals fight over the seat.
Back whichever claimant their superiors bless, and be seen to have waited for the word.
Following the leaders' choice means setting aside one's own judgment, and paying for it whether they chose well or not.
Leads the faith in quiet times, at peace with the seat beside it.
Keep the faith at every naming, wedding and burial, and out of the seat's quarrels.
With nothing pressing, it is easy to grow comfortable and hard to argue for growing.
Serves the faith under its leaders in quiet times.
Serve their flock so faithfully that their superiors cannot pass them over again.
Doing the work well, the leaders' way, goes unnoticed; doing it another way brings trouble.
Heads the leading crew while the seat fails; whatever the seat stops watching is there to take.
Take over whatever the seat has stopped watching, and dig in before it recovers.
Growing too openly now may make the crew the first thing a recovered seat goes after.
Holds a place under the crew's boss while the seat fails.
Climb over the boss's other lieutenants while nobody is enforcing anything.
Climbing means being worth more to the boss or being more of a danger, and the boss can see both.
Heads the crew that has bought some of those who keep order, and works freely while they stay bought.
Keep the bribed officials paid and quiet, and keep proof of every payment in case they turn.
Too many people know about the payments; they hold the crew as much as they shield it.
Holds a place in a crew that has bought protection, without having arranged it.
Use the bought protection while it lasts, and have a way out when it ends.
Living off the bought protection while keeping clear of it is a balance the crew may not allow.
Heads the crew that moves goods on the side while food is short, and the shortage pays well.
Sell food on the side at hungry prices, without becoming the face of the shortage.
Open profit from the hunger makes the crew a target even the bought officials cannot ignore.
Holds a place in a crew that is moving into the black-market food trade.
Get a cut of the black-market food before the boss shuts everyone else out.
A share of it means offering the boss something needed, or taking a small part and no say later.
Heads the crew while money is short, and desperate people are easy to recruit and use.
Sign up the desperate while they are cheap, and keep them once times get better.
A crew built on desperation shrinks when times get better.
Holds a place in a crew while money is short.
Make themselves worth keeping to the crew for reasons that will survive good times.
Staying worth keeping means showing a value that will last, which is hard to show in the middle of hard times.
Heads the crew while rivals fight over the seat and those who keep order look elsewhere.
Move into new rackets while the claimants to the seat are busy with each other.
Either side may turn on the crew to hurt the other, so today's freedom could end without warning.
Holds a place in a crew that is pushing into new ground while the seat is fought over.
Grab their own share of the crew's new ground, so they keep it if the push fails.
Ground taken in a push that fails is the first to be lost when the crew pulls back.
Heads the crew in quiet times, working only where those who keep order choose not to look.
Keep the rackets small and steady enough that the law never bothers to look.
Staying just under notice for too long draws the eye of anyone who looks for exactly that.
Holds a place in a crew in quiet times, with order well kept around it.
Prove to the boss they can be trusted with more, without the law learning their name.
Getting ahead in the crew means showing what one can do, and showing it is how one gets noticed.
Heads the casters while the seat fails; if the seat needs their spells, it now owes them.
Turn every favour the seat now begs of their spells into a right it cannot take back.
Rights won from a weak seat are the first a recovered seat takes back.
Works spells under the senior casters while the seat fails.
Keep working spells for anyone who pays while refusing to be counted on any side.
Staying on no side while everyone suffers is hard to do without looking like a calculation.
Heads the casters among bribe-taking officials, where spells that hide things buy favour and debt.
Stop casting concealments for the crooks before the crooks own them outright.
Once their spells have hidden someone's dealings, getting free of those people is hard.
Works spells under the senior casters, among officials who take bribes.
Take the spellwork their seniors turn down, and ask no questions about why it was refused.
The work the seniors turn down is often turned down for a reason.
Heads the casters while food is short, and any spell that grows or keeps food is suddenly worth a great deal.
Save what food magic can save, and make the seat pay for it in rights.
People fed by spells once will expect it again, and it cannot go on for ever.
Works spells that could help with the shortage, but cannot use them without the seniors' leave.
Offer their spells for the shortage through their seniors, and see their own name on it.
Helping through the seniors limits both what the help can do and who gets the credit.
Heads the casters while money is short, and spellwork is among the first things people stop paying for.
Work out which spells people will still pay for when the coin runs short, and keep those.
Proving the spells are needed may mean casting them so often that they lose their price.
Works spells under the senior casters while money is short and patrons drop away.
Find the plain, needed spellwork that people buy even when they buy nothing else.
The spells people still buy in hard times are the humble ones that pay least.
Heads the casters while rivals fight over the seat, and both sides want their spells.
Refuse every claimant who wants their spells, so whoever takes the seat cannot call them traitors.
Staying out of it means refusing both sides, and both will remember.
Works spells under the senior casters while rivals fight over the seat.
Be useful to whoever wins the seat, and promise nothing to anyone before then.
Serving more than one side means keeping the work small enough that none of them sees a betrayal.
Heads the casters in quiet times; their place is secure and their spells are in demand.
Win more of the seat's work for their spells, and more of everyone else's.
In quiet times the seat slowly hems the casters in with rules; recognition comes with limits.
Works spells under the senior casters in quiet times.
Become the caster people ask for by name, whatever their seniors think of them.
Skill without a senior post leaves the caster at the mercy of whoever decides who may cast.
Heads an old family while the seat fails, and old names count for more when the seat counts for less.
Take back the old family rights the seat stripped away, while it is too weak to refuse.
Old claims that would once have been laughed off are now watched by everyone looking for a grab at power.
Belongs to a lesser family behind the leading one while the seat fails.
Catch up with the greater family while the seat is too busy to keep them apart.
Getting ahead of the greater family now will look like seizing a chance, not earning a place.
Heads an old family while the seat's offices take up more of what the family once did.
Keep the family's name honoured at every feast while the new offices take its old work.
The family's say slowly shrinks beside the offices that run things.
Belongs to a lesser old family, behind the leading one.
Marry, lend or befriend their way into the offices that now run things.
The family has as much say as the offices find it useful to give, whatever its old claim.
